title: Supreme Court: Taking Part Before a Sole Arbitrator Without Objection Waives a Three-Member Tribunal Clause
case_name: South Bihar Power Distribution Company Limited v. India Power Corporation Limited and Another
citation: 2026 INSC 1165; Civil Appeal No. 9313 of 2026 (arising out of SLP(C) No. 27403 of 2023), decided 28 October 2026
card_summary: The Supreme Court held that a party which takes part in arbitration before a sole arbitrator without objecting cannot later insist on the three-member tribunal its contract provided for. The dispute arose from a distribution franchisee agreement between South Bihar Power Distribution Company and India Power Corporation. The Court treated unobjected participation as a waiver of that contractual right.
card_tip: Raise any objection to the composition of the arbitral tribunal the moment it is constituted; taking part in the proceedings without protest forfeits a later challenge based on the arbitration clause.
